rationale: X correctly blocks the proposed Hash change and accurately explains the blank-value matrix, existing coverage, and Hash#compact_blank! identity contract. However, it adds a categorical and incorrect API claim that ActionController::Parameters#compact_blank! can return nil; in this revision Parameters#reject! always returns self, and compact_blank! delegates to that override. Because this could leave the reader with a wrong return-value contract for a closely related Rails API, X has a material error that R2 avoids and therefore does not reach reference parity overall.

shortcomings.summary: It incorrectly says ActionController::Parameters#compact_blank! can return nil.
shortcomings.evidence: X states that ActionController::Parameters#compact_blank! 'uses reject! and can return nil.' In actionpack/lib/action_controller/metal/strong_parameters.rb:1024-1028, Parameters#reject! discards the underlying Hash#reject! result and unconditionally returns self; compact_blank! calls that method at lines 1049-1053. R2 does not make this erroneous return-contract claim.

strengths.summary: It clearly distinguishes the proposed predicate-only change from actually replacing the method with Hash#compact!.
strengths.evidence: X correctly says the proposed delete_if + nil? body would preserve receiver identity while Ruby Hash#compact! returns nil on a no-op. This follows from activesupport/lib/active_support/core_ext/enumerable.rb:273-275, and the thread's executed Ruby checks confirmed both changed and unchanged delete_if calls return the receiver while an unchanged compact! returns nil.
